 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc73667_2"></A>LEGAL INFORMATION </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:14pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Legal address </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Macacha G&uuml;emes 515 - Ciudad Aut&oacute;noma
de Buenos Aires, Argentina. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:14pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Fiscal year </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">No.&nbsp;49
beginning on January&nbsp;1, 2025. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:14pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Main business of the Company </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company&#8217;s purpose shall be to perform, on its own, through third parties or in association with third parties, the survey, exploration and
exploitation of liquid and/or gaseous hydrocarbon fields and other minerals, as well as the industrialization, transportation and commercialization of these products and their direct and indirect <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">by-products,</FONT>
including petrochemical products, chemical products, whether derived from hydrocarbons or not, and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-fossil</FONT> fuels, biofuels and their components, as well as the generation of electrical energy through the
use of hydrocarbons, to which effect it may manufacture, use, purchase, sell, exchange, import or export them. It shall also be the Company&#8217;s purpose the rendering, on its own, through a controlled company or in association with third parties,
of telecommunications services in all forms and modalities authorized by the legislation in force after applying for the relevant licenses as required by the regulatory framework, as well as the production, industrialization, processing,
commercialization, conditioning, transportation and stockpiling of grains and products derived from grains, as well as any other activity complementary to its industrial and commercial business or any activity which may be necessary to attain its
object. To better achieve these purposes, it may set up, become associated with or have an interest in any public or private entity domiciled in Argentina or abroad, within the limits set forth in the Bylaws. </P>

Corporations, Volume A, with the above mentioned Public Registry. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Duration of the Company </U></P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>GENERAL INFORMATION, STRUCTURE AND ORGANIZATION OF THE GROUP&#8217;S BUSINESS </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>General information </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">YPF S.A.
(&#8220;YPF&#8221; or the &#8220;Company&#8221;) is a stock corporation (sociedad an&oacute;nima) incorporated under the Argentine laws, with a registered office at Macacha G&uuml;emes 515, in the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">YPF and its subsidiaries (the &#8220;Group&#8221;) form the leading energy group in Argentina, which operates a fully integrated oil and gas chain with
leading market positions across the domestic Upstream, Midstream and Downstream, LNG and Integrated Gas and New Energies business segments (see Note 6). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Structure and organization of the economic group </U></P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONDENSED INTERIM CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.a) Applicable accounting framework </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The condensed interim
consolidated financial statements of the Company for the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2025, are presented in accordance with IAS 34 &#8220;Interim financial reporting&#8221;. Therefore, they should be read together with the annual
consolidated financial statements of the Company as of December&nbsp;31, 2024 (&#8220;annual consolidated financial statements&#8221;) presented in U.S. dollars and in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the IASB. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">These condensed interim consolidated financial statements corresponding to the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2025, are unaudited. The
Company believes they include all necessary adjustments to reasonably present the results of each period on a basis consistent with the audited annual consolidated financial statements. Net Income for the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30,
2025 does not necessarily reflect the proportion of the Group&#8217;s full-year net income. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.b) Material accounting policies </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The material accounting policies are described in Note 2.b) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The accounting policies adopted in the preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements are consistent with those used in the
preparation of the annual consolidated financial statements, except for the valuation policy for income tax described in Note 19 and the change in the presentation of exchange differences generated by deferred tax described in Note 2.d). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Functional currency </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As mentioned in Note
2.b.1) to the annual consolidated financial statements, YPF has defined the U.S. dollar as its functional currency. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The consolidated financial
statements used by YPF for statutory, legal and regulatory purposes in Argentina are those in pesos and filed with the CNV and approved by the Board of Directors and authorized to be issued on November&nbsp;7, 2025. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Business combinations </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group analyzes
whether the assets acquired and liabilities assumed in a purchase transaction qualify as a business combination in accordance with IFRS 3 &#8220;Business combinations&#8221;. Business combinations are accounted for using the acquisition method,
which requires, among others, the recognition and measurement at fair value of the identifiable assets acquired, the liabilities assumed and any <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-controlling</FONT> interest. The excess of the consideration
transferred over such fair value is recognized as goodwill and the shortfall as a gain in profit or loss for the period. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">When the assets acquired
are not a business, the Group accounts for the transaction as the acquisition of an asset. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Adoption of new standards and interpretations effective as from January&nbsp;1, 2025 </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company has adopted all new and revised standards and interpretations issued by the IASB, relevant to its operations which are of mandatory and
effective application as of September&nbsp;30, 2025, as described in Note 2.b.14) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The adoption of
the amendments mentioned in Note 2.b.14) &#8220;Amendments to IAS 21 - Lack of exchangeability&#8221; section to the annual consolidated financial statements has not had a significant effect on these condensed interim consolidated financial
statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Standards and interpretations issued by the IASB whose application is not mandatory at the closing date of these condensed interim
consolidated financial statements and have not been adopted by the Group</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In accordance with Article 1, Chapter III, Title IV of the CNV rules,
the early application of the IFRS and/or their amendments is not permitted for issuers filing financial statements with the CNV, unless specifically admitted by such agency. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.c) Significant estimates and key sources of estimation uncertainty </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In preparing the financial statements at a certain date, the Group is required to make estimates and assessments affecting the amount of assets and
liabilities recorded and the contingent assets and liabilities disclosed at such date, as well as income and expenses recognized in the fiscal year or period. Actual future profit or loss might differ from the estimates and assessments made at the
date of preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The assumptions relating to the future and other key sources of
uncertainty about the estimates made for the preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements are consistent with those used by the Group in the preparation of the annual consolidated financial statements, which are disclosed
in Note 2.c) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.d) Comparative information </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Amounts and other financial information corresponding to the fiscal year ended December&nbsp;31, 2024 and for the nine-month period ended
September&nbsp;30, 2024 are an integral part of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements and are intended to be read only in relation to these financial statements. Likewise, changes have been made to the comparative figures in
Notes 6 and 26 as mentioned in Note 6. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Additionally, the Group has changed the presentation of exchange differences generated by deferred tax
classifying these items as deferred tax expense (income) in accordance with IAS 12 &#8220;Income taxes&#8221;. Previously, these exchange differences were presented in the &#8220;Other exchange differences, net&#8221; line item under &#8220;Other
financial results&#8221; in the statement of comprehensive income and, from this period, they are presented in the &#8220;Income tax&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income (see Note 19). The purpose of this change is to provide
more useful information and improve the comparability of the Group&#8217;s financial statements with its peers. The comparative information has been restated by reclassifying a gain of 170 and 47 from &#8220;Other financial results&#8221; line item
to &#8220;Income tax&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income for the nine and three-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2024, respectively. This change had no effect on the Group&#8217;s statements of financial position,
statements of changes in shareholders&#8217; equity, cash flows, operating profit or loss and net profit or loss. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B><A NAME="item1toc73667_9"></A>3.</B></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>SEASONALITY OF OPERATIONS </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Historically, the Group&#8217;s results have been subject to seasonal fluctuations throughout the year, particularly as a result of the increase in
natural gas sales during the winter driven by the increased demand in the residential segment. Consequently, the Group is subject to seasonal fluctuations in its sales volumes and prices, with higher sales of natural gas during the winter at higher
prices. </P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>ACQUISITIONS AND DISPOSALS </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The most relevant acquisitions and disposals of companies that took place during the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2025 are described below:
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Acquisition of Mobil Argentina S.A. </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On
December&nbsp;17, 2024, the Company entered into a share purchase and sale agreement with ExxonMobil Argentina Upstream B.V., ExxonMobil Exploration and Production Gemini B.V., and QatarEnergy Argentina Holdings LLC (collectively, the
&#8220;Sellers&#8221;) whereby, subject to the fulfillment of closing conditions set forth in such agreement, YPF acquired 100% of the shares and capital stock of Mobil Argentina S.A. (&#8220;MASA&#8221;). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">MASA owns 54.45% of Sierra Chata unconventional exploitation concession in the Province of Neuqu&eacute;n. Pampa Energ&iacute;a S.A., operator of such
concession, owns the remaining working interest. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;29, 2025 (&#8220;acquisition date&#8221;), after the fulfillment of the closing
conditions, the sale and transfer by the Sellers to YPF of 100% of MASA&#8217;s shares and capital stock was completed. The amount of the transaction was 327 in cash. As of the acquisition date, MASA will continue to operate under the corporate name
SC Gas S.A.U. (&#8220;SC Gas&#8221;), being YPF its sole shareholder. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The transaction described above qualifies as a business combination in
accordance with IFRS 3 and is accounted for using the acquisition method (see Note 2.b) &#8220;Business combinations&#8221; section). The following table details the consideration transferred, the fair values of the identifiable assets acquired and
the liabilities assumed by YPF at the acquisition date: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Acquisition of VMI </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On August&nbsp;6, 2025, the

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On September&nbsp;29, 2025 (&#8220;acquisition date&#8221;), after the fulfillment of the closing conditions, the sale and transfer by Total Austral S.A.

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group&#8217;s activities expose it to a variety of financial risks: Market risk (including exchange rate risk, interest rate risk, and price risk),
liquidity risk and credit risk. Within the Group, risk management functions are conducted in relation to financial risks associated to financial instruments to which the Group is exposed during a certain period or as of a specific date. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2025, there were no significant changes in the administration or policies of risk management

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Most of the Group&#8217;s loans contain market-standard covenants for contracts of this nature, which include financial covenants in respect of the

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>BUSINESS SEGMENT INFORMATION (cont.) </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the current fiscal year, as a consequence of the organizational structure changes in which the New Energies Vice Presidency was created and the Gas
and Power Vice Presidency and the Downstream Vice Presidency were reformulated as the LNG and Integrated Gas Vice Presidency and the Midstream and Downstream Vice Presidency, respectively, the complete management scope of these new business units
was determined. On January&nbsp;1, 2025, these organizational changes resulted in a modification of the composition of the business segments according to how the chief decision maker allocates resources and assesses the performance of these business
segments, creating the New Energies business segment and readjusting the composition and definition of the businesses of the remaining business segments. The changes in the business segments had no impact on the CGUs defined in Note 2.b.5) to the
annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As aforementioned and in Note 5 to the annual consolidated financial statements, the comparative
information for the fiscal year ended December&nbsp;31, 2024 and the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2024 has been restated. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The business
segments structure is organized as follows: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It performs all activities related to the exploration and exploitation of hydrocarbon fields and production of crude oil and natural gas.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;1, 2024, certain assets related to the production of frac sand for well drilling/fracking purposes, which were formerly
included in this business segment, were assigned to Central Administration and Others. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are mainly derived from:
(i)&nbsp;the sale of the produced crude oil to the Midstream and Downstream business segment; (ii)&nbsp;the sale of the produced natural gas to the LNG and Integrated Gas business segment; and (iii)&nbsp;the sale of the natural gas retained in plant
to the Midstream and Downstream business segment. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the aforementioned activities. </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Midstream and Downstream </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;the refining, transportation and commercialization of refined products; (ii)&nbsp;the
production, transportation and commercialization of petrochemical products; (iii)&nbsp;the transportation and commercialization of crude oil; and (iv)&nbsp;the commercialization of specialties for the agribusiness industry and of grains and their <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">by-products.</FONT> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;1, 2025, as a consequence of the organizational changes described
above, the assets related to the natural gas transportation, the conditioning and processing of natural gas retained in plant for the separation and fractionation of gasoline, propane and butane, the storage of the produced natural gas, and the
commercial and technical operation of the LNG regasification terminal in Escobar, which were formerly included in the Gas and Power business segment, were assigned to this business segment. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are mainly derived from the sale of crude oil, refined and petrochemical products, and specialties for agribusiness industry
and grains and their <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">by-products,</FONT> through the businesses of B2C (Retail), B2B (Commercial Networks, Industries, Transportation, Aviation, Agro, Lubricants and Specialties), LPG, Chemicals, International Trade
and Transportation and Sales to Companies. In addition, it obtains revenues from midstream oil, midstream gas and natural gas storage operations and the provision of LNG regasification services. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the aforementioned activities, including the purchase of: (i)&nbsp;crude oil from the Upstream business
segment and third parties; (ii)&nbsp;natural gas to be consumed in the refinery and petrochemical industrial complexes from the LNG and Integrated Gas business segment; and (iii)&nbsp;natural gas retained in plant from the Upstream business segment.
</P> <P STYLE="font-size:100pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:48pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>LNG and Integrated Gas </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;natural gas transportation and commercialization to third parties and to the Midstream and
Downstream business segment; (ii)&nbsp;the separation of natural gas liquids and their fractionation, storage and transportation for the production of ethane, propane, butane and gasoline, and its commercialization, through our investment in joint
venture Mega; and (iii)&nbsp;the development of LNG capacity. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;1, 2025, as a consequence of the organizational changes
described above, the assets related to the natural gas transportation, the conditioning and processing of natural gas retained in plant for the separation and fractionation of gasoline, propane and butane, the storage of the produced natural gas,
and the commercial and technical operation of the LNG regasification terminal in Escobar, which were formerly included in the Gas and Power business segment, were assigned to the Midstream and Downstream business segment. Furthermore, the assets
related to the distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas, the generation of conventional thermal electric power and renewable energy, and the production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers through our investments in
associates and joint ventures, which were formerly included in the Gas and Power business segment, were assigned to the New Energies business segment. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are mainly derived from the commercialization of natural gas as producers to third parties and to the Midstream and
Downstream and the New Energies business segments. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the aforementioned activities, including the
purchase of natural gas from the Upstream business segment. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>New Energies </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;1, 2025, as a consequence of the organizational changes described above, the New Energies Vice Presidency was created and
during the current fiscal year the complete management scope of this new business unit was determined. As of that date, the assets related to the distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas, the generation of conventional thermal
electric power and renewable energy and the production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers through our investments in associates and joint ventures, which were formerly included in the Gas and Power business segment, were assigned to this
business segment. In addition, the assets related to the provision of research and development services of technology applied to the hydrocarbon industry through our subsidiary <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Y-TEC,</FONT> previously included in
Central Administration and Others, were assigned to this business segment. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;the definition
and development of the new energy portfolio; (ii)&nbsp;the definition and development of sustainability and energy transitions programs; (iii)&nbsp;the distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas; and (iv)&nbsp;the provision of
research and development services of technology applied to the hydrocarbon industry through our subsidiary <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Y-TEC.</FONT> Furthermore, through our investments in associates and joint ventures, this business segment
performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;the generation of conventional thermal electric power and renewable energy; and (ii)&nbsp;the production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are mainly derived from the sale of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the aforementioned activities, including the purchase of natural gas from the LNG and Integrated Gas
business segment. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Central Administration and Others </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It includes the remaining activities performed by the Group that do not fall within the aforementioned business segments and which are not
reporting business segments, mainly comprising revenues, expenses and assets related to: (i)&nbsp;corporate administrative; (ii)&nbsp;the production of frac sand for well drilling/fracking purposes; and (iii)&nbsp;the construction activities through
our subsidiary AESA. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;1, 2024, certain assets related to the production of frac sand for well drilling/fracking purposes,
which were formerly included in the Upstream business segment, were assigned to Central Administration and Others. In addition, on January&nbsp;1, 2025, as a consequence of the organizational changes described above, the assets related to the
provision of research and development services of technology applied to the hydrocarbon industry through our subsidiary <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Y-TEC,</FONT> previously included in Central Administration and Others, were assigned to the New
Energies business segment. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Sales between business segments were made at internal transfer prices established by the Group, which approximately
reflect domestic market prices. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Operating profit or loss and assets of each business segment have been determined after consolidation adjustments.

Ingenier&iacute;a SIMA S.A., the transfer of 100% of the rights and obligations of YPF in such exploitation concessions in favor of Bentia and Ingenier&iacute;a SIMA S.A. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Al Norte de la Dorsal, Oct&oacute;gono and Dad&iacute;n</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;9, 2025, Decree No.&nbsp;380/2025 was published in the Official Gazette of the Province of Neuqu&eacute;n, which authorized the transfer of
100% of YPF&#8217;s rights and obligations in &#8220;Al Norte de la Dorsal&#8221; and &#8220;Oct&oacute;gono&#8221; exploitation concessions in favor of Bentia. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;10, 2025, after the fulfillment of the closing conditions by YPF and Bentia related to &#8220;Al Norte de la Dorsal&#8221; and
&#8220;Oct&oacute;gono&#8221; exploitation concessions, the transfer of 100% of the rights and obligations of YPF in such exploitation concessions in favor of Bentia was formalized. As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated
financial statements, YPF and Bentia entered into a transitory operation agreement for the &#8220;Dad&iacute;n&#8221; exploitation concession, pending the transfer regarding this concession by the Province of Neuqu&eacute;n. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Cerro Piedra - Cerro Guadal Norte, Barranca Yankowsky, Los Monos, El Guadal - Lomas del Cuy, Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Vasco, Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Yatel,
Pico Truncado - El Cord&oacute;n, Los Perales - Las Mesetas, Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Le&oacute;n - Meseta Espinosa and Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n de la Escondida - Las Heras </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;2, 2025, YPF signed a Memorandum of Understanding (&#8220;MOU&#8221;) with the Province of Santa Cruz and Fomicruz S.E.
(&#8220;Fomicruz&#8221;) for the purpose of establishing the general terms and conditions upon which the assignment by YPF to Fomicruz of the exploitation concessions &#8220;Cerro Piedra - Cerro Guadal Norte&#8221;, &#8220;Barranca Yankowsky&#8221;,
&#8220;Los Monos&#8221;, &#8220;El Guadal - Lomas del Cuy&#8221;, &#8220;Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Vasco&#8221;, &#8220;Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Yatel&#8221;, &#8220;Pico Truncado - El Cord&oacute;n&#8221;, &#8220;Los Perales - Las Mesetas&#8221;,
&#8220;Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Le&oacute;n - Meseta Espinosa&#8221;, &#8220;Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n de la Escondida - Las Heras&#8221; and the transportation concessions associated with such concessions will be negotiated. The aforementioned MOU,
subject to approval by YPF&#8217;s Board of Directors and the issuance of the corresponding decree by the Province of Santa Cruz, was approved by YPF&#8217;s Board of Directors on April&nbsp;9, 2025 and Decree No.&nbsp;376/2025 was issued by the
Province of Santa Cruz on May&nbsp;6, 2025. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;2, 2025, YPF and Fomicruz signed an assignment agreement for the transfer of 100% of the
participating interest in the aforementioned exploitation and transportation concessions. The transfer was approved by Decree No.&nbsp;539/2025 published in the Official Gazette of the Province of Santa Cruz on June&nbsp;18, 2025. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;19, 2025, YPF and Fomicruz executed the notarial deed, thereby formalizing and perfecting the aforementioned assignment. Additionally, YPF
and Fomicruz signed a transitory operation agreement for all the assigned exploitation concessions, pursuant to which YPF shall continue to operate said concessions for a maximum period of up to 6 months. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>El Port&oacute;n (Mendoza - Neuqu&eacute;n), Chihuido de la Salina, Altiplanicie del Pay&uacute;n, Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Amarillo, Chihuido de la
Salina Sur and Confluencia Sur </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On February&nbsp;20, 2025, Resolution No.&nbsp;28/2025 of the Ministry of Energy and Environment was published in
the Official Gazette of the Province of Mendoza, which authorized the transfer of 100% of YPF&#8217;s rights and obligations in &#8220;El Port&oacute;n&#8221;, &#8220;Chihuido de la Salina&#8221;, &#8220;Altiplanicie del Pay&uacute;n&#8221;,
&#8220;Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Amarillo&#8221;, &#8220;Chihuido de la Salina Sur&#8221; and &#8220;Confluencia Sur&#8221; exploitation concessions in favor of Consorcio Quintana and Compa&ntilde;&iacute;a TSB S.A. (&#8220;TSB&#8221;). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;19, 2025, after the fulfillment of the closing conditions by YPF, Consorcio Quintana and TSB, the transfer of 100% of the rights and
obligations of YPF in such exploitation concessions in favor of Consorcio Quintana and TSB was formalized with effective date as of July&nbsp;1, 2025. As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, YPF,
Consorcio Quintana and TSB, entered into a transitory operation agreement for the &#8220;El Port&oacute;n&#8221; exploitation concession, pending the authorization by the Province of Neuqu&eacute;n of the transfer regarding this concession. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Se&ntilde;al Picada - Punta Barda</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>El Tordillo, Puesto Quiroga and La Tapera</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;19, 2025 YPF signed an agreement that establishes the terms and conditions for the reversion of the &#8220;Restinga Al&iacute;&#8221;
exploitation concession, located in the Province of Chubut. On July&nbsp;24, 2025 the Legislature of the Province of Chubut approved the agreement through Law XVII No.&nbsp;162/2025, which was enacted on August&nbsp;1, 2025 and published in the
Official Gazette of the Province of Chubut on August&nbsp;7, 2025. Additionally, as of the issuance date of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the reversion agreement is subject to the approval by decree of the Executive
Branch of the Province of Chubut. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the Company has signed
assignment agreements for certain groups of assets as held for sale that are subject to closing conditions mainly related to regulatory and provincial approvals, for which the Company is taking the necessary steps to close; and it is highly probable
that these assets will be disposed. In addition, the Company maintains groups of assets as held for sale for which agreements have not yet been signed but continues in negotiations with third parties for their disposal or reversal. The delay in the
fulfillment of the plan for the disposal of mature fields is due to the complexity of the negotiations, which is beyond the Company&#8217;s control. As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the Company
considers that the disposal of such assets continues to be highly probable during 2025. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Considering that the assets classified as held for sale are measured at the lower of their carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell (&#8220;fair
value&#8221;), the Company evaluates the changes in fair value, recognizing a profit up to the limit of the impairment loss previously recognized or an impairment loss in addition to that previously recognized for such changes, (see Note 2.b.13) to
the annual consolidated financial statements). The carrying amount of the assets held for sale and associated liabilities may be adjusted in future periods depending on the results of the disposal process carry out by YPF and the economic
consideration to be agreed with third parties for such assets. </P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>INCOME TAX (cont.) </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The effective income tax rate projected at the end of the fiscal year amounts to 129.01%. The variation
in this rate compared to the effective rate as of December&nbsp;31, 2024 (see Note 18 to the annual consolidated financial statements) is mainly explained by the impact of the estimation of certain macroeconomic variables in the measurement of
property, plant, and equipment for accounting and tax purposes, which generates an increase in deferred income tax liability related to those assets. The accounting measurement of property, plant and equipment is based on the Company&#8217;s
functional currency according to IFRS (see Note 2.b)), while the tax measurement is based on inflation-adjusted pesos. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of September&nbsp;30, 2025
and December&nbsp;31, 2024, the causes that generated charges within &#8220;Other comprehensive income&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income did not generate temporary differences subject to income tax. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of September&nbsp;30, 2025 and December&nbsp;31, 2024 the Group has classified as deferred tax asset 4 and 330, respectively, and as deferred tax
liability 389 and 90, respectively, all of which arise from the net deferred tax balances of each of the individual companies included in these condensed interim consolidated financial statements. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of September&nbsp;30, 2025, the Company&#8217;s capital amounts to 3,928 and treasury shares amount to 5 represented by 393,312,793 book-entry shares
of common stock and divided into four classes of shares (A, B, C and D), with a par value of 10 pesos and 1 vote per share. These shares are fully subscribed, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">paid-in</FONT> and authorized for stock exchange listing.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of September&nbsp;30, 2025, there are 3,764 Class&nbsp;A outstanding shares. As long as any Class&nbsp;A share remains outstanding, the
affirmative vote of the Argentine Government is required for: (i)&nbsp;mergers; (ii) acquisitions of more than 50% of YPF shares in an agreed or hostile bid; (iii)&nbsp;transfers of all the YPF&#8217;s exploitation and exploration rights;
(iv)&nbsp;the voluntary dissolution of YPF; (v)&nbsp;change of corporate and/or tax address outside Argentina; or (vi)&nbsp;make an acquisition that would result in the purchaser holding 15% or more of the Company&#8217;s capital stock, or 20% or
more of the outstanding Class&nbsp;D shares. Items (iii)&nbsp;and (iv) also require prior approval by the Argentine Congress. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the nine-month
periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2025 and 2024, the Company has not repurchased any of its own shares. Furthermore, on October&nbsp;14, 2025, the Company repurchased 343,654 of its own shares issued for an amount of 10 for purposes of compliance
with the share-based benefit plans. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;30, 2025, the General Shareholders&#8217; Meeting was held, which approved the statutory financial
statements of YPF (see Note 2.b)) corresponding to the year ended on December&nbsp;31, 2024 and, additionally, approved the following in relation to the retained earnings: (i)&nbsp;completely release the reserve for purchase of treasury shares and
the reserve for investments; (ii)&nbsp;allocate the amount of 34,205&nbsp;million of pesos (US$ 33 million) to appropriate a reserve for purchase of treasury shares; and (iii)&nbsp;allocate the amount of 6,787,343&nbsp;million of pesos (US$ 6,587
million) to appropriate a reserve for investments. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc73667_39"></A>33. EARNINGS PER SHARE </B></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>34.b.1) Contentious claims </B></P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

&#8211; Eton Park Capital Management, L.P., Eton Park Master Fund, LTD. and Eton Park Fund, L.P. (collectively, &#8220;Eton Park&#8221;, and together with Petersen, the &#8220;Plaintiffs&#8221;) </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;30, 2025, the District Court granted Plaintiffs&#8217; turnover motion, ordering the Republic to: (i)&nbsp;transfer its Class&nbsp;D shares
of YPF to a global custody account at the Bank of New York Mellon (&#8220;BNYM&#8221;) in New York within 14 days of the date of the order; and (ii)&nbsp;instruct BNYM to initiate a transfer of the Republic&#8217;s ownership interests in its
Class&nbsp;D shares of YPF to Plaintiffs or their designees within one business day of the date on which the shares are deposited into the account. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Also on June&nbsp;30, 2025, in proceedings brought by Bainbridge Fund Ltd. against the Republic, the District Court issued a similar order directing the
Republic to turn over its Class&nbsp;A and Class&nbsp;D shares of YPF. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Republic filed motions to stay the June&nbsp;30, 2025 turnover orders
pending its appeal of those orders, which were denied by the District Court. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;10, 2025, the Republic filed with the Court of Appeals:
(i)&nbsp;notices of appeal of the June&nbsp;30, 2025 turnover orders in both Plaintiffs&#8217; and Bainbridge Fund Ltd.&#8217;s proceedings; and (ii)&nbsp;emergency motions for a stay pending appeal of the June&nbsp;30, 2025 turnover orders and an
immediate administrative stay. On July&nbsp;15, 2025, the Court of Appeals granted a temporary administrative stay of the turnover orders pending resolution of the stay motions. On August&nbsp;15, 2025, the Court of Appeals granted a stay pending
resolution of the Republic&#8217;s appeal of the June&nbsp;30, 2025 turnover orders. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">YPF is not a party to the aforementioned turnover proceedings.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;29, 2025, the District Court lifted the stay of alter ego discovery entered on November&nbsp;15, 2024, including regarding YPF. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On September&nbsp;17, 2025, the District Court denied YPF&#8217;s request to permanently enjoin Plaintiffs from pursuing recovery from YPF in connection
with their September&nbsp;15, 2023 final judgment against the Republic and ordered Plaintiffs and YPF to continue with the discovery process. It should be noted that the District Court&#8217;s decision does not decide the question of whether YPF is
an alter ego of the Republic, which YPF strongly denies. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On October&nbsp;1, 2025, YPF filed a motion for reconsideration of the September&nbsp;17,
2025 order with the District Court, as well as a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-motion</FONT> letter requesting to stay discovery from YPF. On October&nbsp;6, 2025, Plaintiffs submitted a letter opposing a discovery stay and YPF replied on
October&nbsp;7, 2025. On October&nbsp;15, 2025, Plaintiffs filed an opposition to YPF&#8217;s motion for reconsideration. On October&nbsp;16, 2025, the District Court held a conference regarding YPF&#8217;s request to stay alter ego discovery from
YPF. The Court granted the request for a stay pending resolution of YPF&#8217;s reconsideration motion. On October&nbsp;17, 2025, YPF filed its notice of appeal of the September&nbsp;17, 2025 order. On October&nbsp;22, 2025, YPF filed its reply to
Plaintiffs&#8217; opposition of October&nbsp;15, 2025. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">With respect to the appeal of the final judgment issued on September&nbsp;15, 2023, the Court
of Appeals held oral argument on October&nbsp;29, 2025. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:50pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc73667_42"></A>36. MAIN REGULATIONS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.a) Regulations applicable to the hydrocarbon industry </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During
the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2025, there were no significant updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 36.a) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.b) Regulations applicable to the Midstream and Downstream business segment </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Notes 36.b), 36.c.1), 36.c.2) and 36.c.4) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the
nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2025, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.b.1) Regulatory framework associated with the LPG industry </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;3, 2025, Decree No.&nbsp;446/2025 was published modifying the LPG Law, which: (i)&nbsp;confirms the free import of LPG; (ii)&nbsp;removes the
authority of the PEN to impose restrictions on prices and commercialization conditions; and (iii)&nbsp;limits the intervention of the SE in the LPG industry to technical and safety aspects. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.c) Regulations applicable to the LNG and Integrated Gas business segment </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Notes 36.c.1) and 36.c.2) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the nine-month period ended
September&nbsp;30, 2025, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.c.1) Exports of natural gas and LNG </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>LNG</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;21, 2025, SE Resolution
No.&nbsp;157/2025 was published, which approved the declaration of sufficiency of natural gas resources in Argentina that would supply local demand and LNG export projects for 63 years, which must be updated by the SE at least every 5 years. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.d) Regulations applicable to the New Energies business segment </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL">Updates to
the regulatory framework described in Notes 36.c.3), 36.c.5) and 36.c.6) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2025, are described below: </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.d.1) Regulatory requirements applicable to natural gas distribution </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Tariff schemes and tariff renegotiations</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">ENARGAS, through several resolutions, approved the transition tariff schemes to be applied by Metrogas until the rates resulting from the RQT came into
force in accordance with the provisions of Decree No.&nbsp;55/2023. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;30, 2025, ENARGAS Resolution No.&nbsp;257/2025 was published, which
approved: (i)&nbsp;the RQT corresponding to Metrogas; (ii)&nbsp;the segmentation of residential users; (iii)&nbsp;the investment plans for the five-year period 2025&#8212;2030; and (iv)&nbsp;the initial tariff scheme and the schemes of rates and
charges corresponding to Metrogas effective as from May&nbsp;1, 2025. The increase expected as a result of the RQT process will be effective in 31 consecutive monthly increases, which recognizes a cost for the deferral at a real weighted average
cost of the capital employed rate in pesos of 7.64% and establishes that the increase in distribution tariffs for May 2025 applicable to residential users and general service customers will be 3%. The application of the remaining increase derived
from the RQT will be completed in the remaining 30 installments, plus the recognition of the cost of the aforementioned deferral. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;5,
2025, SE Resolution No.&nbsp;241/2025 was published, which established that the transportation and distribution tariffs will be adjusted on a monthly basis according to the variations in the indexes established by ENARGAS in the RQT, which
correspond to the variation in equal parts of the IPC and the Internal Wholesale Price Index (&#8220;IPIM&#8221; by its acronym in Spanish) published by the INDEC. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="right">HORACIO DANIEL MAR&Iacute;N </P>

<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;6, 2025, ENARGAS Resolution No.&nbsp;363/2025 was published, which approved: (i)&nbsp;the
methodology for the monthly adjustment of tariffs; and (ii)&nbsp;the tariff charts to be applied by Metrogas effective as from June&nbsp;6, 2025. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">ENARGAS, through several resolutions, approved the tariff schemes to be applied by Metrogas on a monthly basis within the framework of the RQT in
accordance with the provisions of ENARGAS Resolution No.&nbsp;363/2025. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Procedure for the compensation of the lower revenues received by natural
gas distributors from their users</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;31, 2025, SE Resolution No.&nbsp;24/2025 repealed as from February&nbsp;1, 2025 MINEM
Resolution No. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">508-E/2017,</FONT> which established the procedure to compensate natural gas distributors for lower revenues due to benefits and/or bonuses and higher costs of UNG and unified the compensation
mechanisms for lower revenues received as a consequence of the application of incentive programs involving bonuses on the price of natural gas in the PIST. The amounts to be compensated will be deducted from the amounts to be paid by distributors to
natural gas producers and will be directly compensated by the SE through the Plan GasAr 2023-2028. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.d.2) Regulatory framework associated with electric power
generation </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;7, 2025, Decree No.&nbsp;450/2025 was published, which approves the following amendments to the Regulatory Framework
associated with electric power generation: (i)&nbsp;maximum competition and free contracting is guaranteed to generators; (ii)&nbsp;supply contracts will be freely negotiated between the parties; (iii)&nbsp;the figure of &#8220;storer&#8221; is
introduced as the owner of energy storage facilities; (iv)&nbsp;the figure of &#8220;free user&#8221; is introduced, who, together with large users, may contract independently and for own consumption the energy supply; (v)&nbsp;allows the PEN to
authorize generators, distributors and/or large users to build, at their exclusive cost and to satisfy their own needs, a line and/or extension of the transmission grid, which will not provide a public transportation service; and (vi)&nbsp;the
extensions of the Argentine Electricity Grid (&#8220;SADI&#8221;, by its acronym in Spanish) may be of free initiative and at the own risk of whoever executes them. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>CAMMESA</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The SE, through several complementary
notes to SE Resolution No.&nbsp;21/2025, informed CAMMESA of the &#8220;Guidelines for the Standardization of the WEM and its Progressive Adaptation&#8221;, which details among others the modifications foreseen for the management of fuels, the
determination of prices and the operation of the term market and the spot market, approved by SE Resolution No.&nbsp;400/2025 and applicable as from November&nbsp;1, 2025. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.d.3) Decree No.&nbsp;55/2023 &#8220;Emergency in the National Energy Sector&#8221; </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;2, 2025, Decree No.&nbsp;370/2025 was published extending the emergency of the national energy sector until July&nbsp;9, 2026. It also
provided for the extension of the intervention of ENRE and ENARGAS until July&nbsp;9, 2026 or until the constitution, commencement and appointment of the members of the Board of Directors of the National Gas and Electricity Regulatory Agency. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;7, 2025, Decree No.&nbsp;452/2025 was published, establishing the National Gas and Electricity Regulatory Agency and granting a term of 180
days for its commencement of operations. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.e) Incentive programs for hydrocarbon production </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 36.d) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the nine-month period ended
September&nbsp;30, 2025, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.e.1) Incentive programs for natural gas production </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Plan for Reinsurance and Promotion of Federal Hydrocarbon Production Domestic Self-Sufficiency, Exports, Imports Substitution and the Expansion of the
Transportation System for all Hydrocarbon Basins in the Country 2023-2028 (&#8220;Plan GasAr 2023-2028&#8221;)</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The SE, through several
resolutions, approves the natural gas prices at the PIST to be passed-through to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">end-users</FONT> in connection with current contracts entered into within the framework of the Plan GasAr 2023-2028. </P>

Export duties </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Agricultural products</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On
July&nbsp;31, 2025, Decree No.&nbsp;526/2025 was published, which established the permanent reduction in export duties established by Decree No.&nbsp;38/2025. As from such date, the rates are set at 26% for soybean, 24.5% for soybean byproducts such
as soybean oil and soybean meal, and 9.5% for grains such as wheat, corn and sorghum. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.i) Regulations related to the Foreign Exchange Market </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 36.h) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the nine-month period ended
September&nbsp;30, 2025, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;11, 2025, the Argentine Government announced measures to loosen the foreign exchange
regime and reinforce the monetary framework. By virtue of this, the BCRA implemented a new foreign exchange regime in which certain restrictions to access the Foreign Exchange Market were eliminated. The following are the main measures: (i)&nbsp;the
&#8220;crawling peg&#8221; adjustment mechanism is eliminated and the dollar exchange rate in the Foreign Exchange Market may fluctuate in a range between 1,000 pesos and 1,400 pesos, whose limits will be increased at a rate of 1% per month;
(ii)&nbsp;the &#8220;blend&#8221; dollar was eliminated (see Note 36.i) &#8220;Export Increase Program&#8221; section); (iii) certain foreign exchange restrictions to individuals for the purchase of foreign currency were eliminated; (iv)&nbsp;access
to the Foreign Exchange Market is allowed without prior approval of the BCRA for the payment of dividends to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-resident</FONT> shareholders accrued as from fiscal years beginning on or after January&nbsp;1, 2025;
and (v)&nbsp;the terms for the payment of foreign trade transactions are flexibilized, eliminating the schedule established by the BCRA for access to the Foreign Exchange Market without prior approval for the payment of imports of goods with customs
entry registration as from December&nbsp;13, 2023 and of services rendered and/or accrued as from such date. </P>

</P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc73667_44"></A>38. EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLANS AND SIMILAR OBLIGATIONS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Note 38 to the annual consolidated financial statements describes the main characteristics and accounting treatment for employee benefit plans and

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense related to the Retirement Plan was 3 and 3 for the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Short-term benefit programs </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount
charged to expense related to the short-term benefit programs was 146 and 165 for the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2025 and 2024, respectively. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Share-based benefit plans </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of
September&nbsp;30, 2025, there are 4.6&nbsp;million number of PSARs outstanding with and a weighted average fair value of US$ 10.87 per PSARs. The amount charged to expense in relation with Value Generation Plan was a recovery of 7 due to changes in
the fair value estimate of the option and a loss of 7, for the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2025 and 2024, respectively. As of December&nbsp;31, 2024, weighted average fair value was US$ 28.6 per PSARs. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense in relation with the remaining share-based benefit plans was 9 and 5 to be settled in equity instruments, for the nine-month
periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2025 and 2024, respectively, and 1 and 8 to be settled in cash, for the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2025 and 2024, respectively. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Note 2.b.11) to the annual consolidated financial statements describes the accounting policies for share-based benefit plans. Repurchases of treasury
shares are disclosed in Note 32. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:50pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

export them. It shall also be the Company&#8217;s purpose the rendering, on its own, through a controlled company or in association with third parties, of telecommunications services in all forms and modalities authorized by the legislation in force
after applying for the relevant licenses as required by the regulatory framework, as well as the production, industrialization, processing, commercialization, conditioning, transportation and stockpiling of grains and products derived from grains,
as well as any other activity complementary to its industrial and commercial business or any activity which may be necessary to attain its object. To better achieve these purposes, it may set up, become associated with or have an interest in any

CONDENSED INTERIM CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>2.a) Applicable accounting framework </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The condensed interim consolidated financial statements of the Company for the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2025, are presented in
accordance with IAS 34 &#8220;Interim financial reporting&#8221;. Therefore, they should be read together with the annual consolidated financial statements of the Company as of December&nbsp;31, 2024 (&#8220;annual consolidated financial
statements&#8221;) presented in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the IASB. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Moreover, some additional information required by
the LGS and/or CNV&#8217;s Rules have been included. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">These condensed interim consolidated financial statements corresponding to the nine-month period
ended September&nbsp;30, 2025, are unaudited. The Company believes they include all necessary adjustments to reasonably present the results of each period on a basis consistent with the audited annual consolidated financial statements. Net Income
for the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2025 does not necessarily reflect the proportion of the Group&#8217;s full-year net income. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>2.b) Material accounting policies </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The material
accounting policies are described in Note 2.b) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The accounting policies adopted in the preparation of
these condensed interim consolidated financial statements are consistent with those used in the preparation of the annual consolidated financial statements, except for the valuation policy for income tax described in Note 19 and the change in the
presentation of exchange differences generated by deferred tax described in Note 2.d). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Functional and presentation currency</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As mentioned in Note 2.b.1) to the annual consolidated financial statements, YPF has defined the U.S. dollar as its functional currency. Additionally, in
accordance with the provisions of the LGS and the CNV rules, the Company must present its financial statements in pesos. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Business combinations</U>
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group analyzes whether the assets acquired and liabilities assumed in a purchase transaction qualify as a business combination in accordance with
IFRS 3 &#8220;Business combinations&#8221;. Business combinations are accounted for using the acquisition method, which requires, among others, the recognition and measurement at fair value of the identifiable assets acquired, the liabilities
assumed and any <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-controlling</FONT> interest. The excess of the consideration transferred over such fair value is recognized as goodwill and the shortfall as a gain in profit or loss for the period. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">When the assets acquired are not a business, the Group accounts for the transaction as the acquisition of an asset. </P>

classifying these items as deferred tax expense (income) in accordance with IAS 12 &#8220;Income taxes&#8221;. Previously, these exchange differences were presented in the &#8220;Other exchange differences, net&#8221; line item under &#8220;Other
financial results&#8221; in the statement of comprehensive income and, from this period, they are presented in the &#8220;Income tax&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income (see Note 19). The purpose of this change is to provide
more useful information and improve the comparability of the Group&#8217;s financial statements with its peers. The comparative information has been restated by reclassifying a gain of 148,702 and 43,699 from &#8220;Other financial results&#8221;
line item to &#8220;Income tax&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income for the nine and three-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2024, respectively. This change had no effect on the Group&#8217;s statements of financial
position, statements of changes in shareholders&#8217; equity, cash flows, operating profit or loss and net profit or loss. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item273667_9"></A>3. <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The most relevant acquisitions and disposals of companies that took place during the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2025 are described below:
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Acquisition of Mobil Argentina S.A.</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On
December&nbsp;17, 2024, the Company entered into a share purchase and sale agreement with ExxonMobil Argentina Upstream B.V., ExxonMobil Exploration and Production Gemini B.V., and QatarEnergy Argentina Holdings LLC (collectively, the
&#8220;Sellers&#8221;) whereby, subject to the fulfillment of closing conditions set forth in such agreement, YPF acquired 100% of the shares and capital stock of Mobil Argentina S.A. (&#8220;MASA&#8221;). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">MASA owns 54.45% of Sierra Chata unconventional exploitation concession in the Province of Neuqu&eacute;n. Pampa Energ&iacute;a S.A., operator of such
concession, owns the remaining working interest. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;29, 2025 (&#8220;acquisition date&#8221;), after the fulfillment of the closing
conditions, the sale and transfer by the Sellers to YPF of 100% of MASA&#8217;s shares and capital stock was completed. The amount of the transaction was US$ 327&nbsp;million in cash. As of the acquisition date, MASA will continue to operate under
the corporate name SC Gas S.A.U. (&#8220;SC Gas&#8221;), being YPF its sole shareholder. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The transaction described above qualifies as a business

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Sale of equity participation in YPF Brasil Com&eacute;rcio Derivado de Petr&oacute;leo Ltda. (&#8220;YPF Brasil&#8221;)</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;31, 2025, after the fulfillment of the closing conditions of the share purchase and sale agreement of the subsidiary YPF Brasil, the sale
and transfer by YPF to the GMZ HOLDING LTDA. and IGP HOLDING PARTICIPA&Ccedil;&Otilde;ES S.A., with the intervention of USIQU&Iacute;MICA DO BRASIL LTDA. as guarantor of the transaction, of 100% of the shares and capital stock of YPF Brasil was
completed. The sale price of the transaction was US$ 2.3&nbsp;million. See Note 3 &#8220;Sale of equity participation in YPF Brasil&#8221; section to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Based on the closing of the aforementioned share purchase and sale agreement and considering the fair value of the assets and liabilities of YPF Brasil
classified as held for sale, as of the closing date of the transaction, the result from the sale did not have significant effects. In addition, the translation differences accumulated in the &#8220;Other comprehensive income&#8221; account and
reclassified to the profit or loss due to the loss of control of the subsidiary amounted to a loss of 851. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Acquisition of equity participation of
OLCLP</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;31, 2025, the Company entered into a share purchase and sale agreement with Tecpetrol S.A. whereby, subject to the
fulfillment of closing conditions set forth in such agreement, YPF acquired 15% of the shares and capital stock of OLCLP joint venture. On June&nbsp;4, 2025 (&#8220;acquisition date&#8221;), after the fulfillment of the closing conditions, the sale
and transfer by Tecpetrol S.A. to YPF of 15% of the shares and capital stock of OLCLP was completed. </P>

<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Acquisition of Refinor</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On October&nbsp;28, 2025, the Company entered into a share purchase and sale agreement with Hidrocarburos del Norte S.A. whereby YPF acquired 50% of the
shares and capital stock of Refinor joint venture. As of that date YPF, which owned 50% of the capital stock of Refinor prior to aforementioned share purchase and sale agreement, is the sole owner and shareholder of 100% of capital stock of Refinor.
The amount of the transaction was US$ 25.2&nbsp;million. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The transaction described above qualifies as a business combination achieved in stages in
accordance with IFRS 3. As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements and due to the recent closing of the transaction, the Group is in the process of determining the accounting impact of this transaction.
Consequently, it is not possible to disclose the information required by IFRS 3 in relation to the measurement of the assets acquired and liabilities assumed at their fair values at the acquisition date and the impact on the Group&#8217;s results
and cash flows from the recording of this acquisition. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item273667_11"></A>5. &#8201;FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group&#8217;s activities expose it to a variety of financial risks: Market risk (including exchange rate risk, interest rate risk, and price risk),
liquidity risk and credit risk. Within the Group, risk management functions are conducted in relation to financial risks associated to financial instruments to which the Group is exposed during a certain period or as of a specific date. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2025, there were no significant changes in the administration or policies of risk management
implemented by the Group as described in Note 4 to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE CELLSPACING="0" CELLPADDING="0" WIDTH="100%" BORDER="0" STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt" ALIGN="center">

<TD WIDTH="2%"></TD>

<TD VALIGN="bottom" WIDTH="1%"></TD>
