<TR STYLE="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt">
<TD VALIGN="top"><FONT STYLE="font-size:10pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman">&#9679;</FONT></FONT></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom"><B>Liquidity risk management</B></TD></TR>
</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Most of the Group&#8217;s loans contain market-standard covenants for contracts of this nature, which include financial
covenants in respect of the Group&#8217;s leverage ratio and debt service coverage ratio, and events of defaults triggered by materially adverse judgements, among others. See Notes 17, 33 and 34 to the annual consolidated financial statements and
Notes 18 and 34. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group monitors compliance with covenants on a quarterly basis. As of September&nbsp;30, 2025, the Group is in compliance with
its covenants. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item273667_12"></A>6. &#8201;BUSINESS SEGMENT INFORMATION </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The different business segments in which the Group&#8217;s organization is structured consider the different activities from which the Group can obtain
revenues and incur expenses. Such organizational structure is based on the way in which the chief decision maker analyzes the main operating and financial magnitudes for making decisions about resource allocation and performance assessment, also
considering the business strategy of the Group. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Business segment information is presented in U.S. dollars, the functional currency of the Company
(see Note 2.b)), consistently with the manner of reporting the information used by the chief decision maker to allocate resources and assess business segment performance. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:120pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

Argentine pesos, or as otherwise indicated) </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>6. &#8201;BUSINESS SEGMENT INFORMATION (cont.) </B></P>
<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the current fiscal year, as a consequence of the organizational structure changes in which the New
Energies Vice Presidency was created, and the Gas and Power Vice Presidency and the Downstream Vice Presidency were reformulated as the LNG and Integrated Gas Vice Presidency and the Midstream and Downstream Vice Presidency respectively, the
complete management scope of these new business units was determined. On January&nbsp;1, 2025, these organizational changes resulted in a modification of the composition of the business segments according to how the chief decision maker allocates
resources and assesses the performance of these business segments, creating the New Energies business segment and readjusting the composition and definition of the businesses of the remaining business segments. The changes in the business segments
had no impact on the CGUs defined in Note 2.b.5) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As aforementioned and in Note 5 to the annual
consolidated financial statements, the comparative information for the fiscal year ended December&nbsp;31, 2024 and the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2024 has been restated. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The business segments structure is organized as follows: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Upstream </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It performs all activities related to the exploration and exploitation of hydrocarbon fields and production of crude oil and natural gas.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;1, 2024, certain assets related to the production of frac sand for well drilling/fracking purposes, which were formerly
included in this business segment, were assigned to Central Administration and Others. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are mainly derived from:
(i)&nbsp;the sale of the produced crude oil to the Midstream and Downstream business segment; (ii)&nbsp;the sale of the produced natural gas to the LNG and Integrated Gas business segment; and (iii)&nbsp;the sale of the natural gas retained in plant
to the Midstream and Downstream business segment. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the aforementioned activities. </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Midstream and Downstream </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;the refining, transportation and commercialization of refined products; (ii)&nbsp;the
production, transportation and commercialization of petrochemical products; (iii)&nbsp;the transportation and commercialization of crude oil; and (iv)&nbsp;the commercialization of specialties for the agribusiness industry and of grains and their <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">by-products.</FONT> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;1, 2025, as a consequence of the organizational changes described
above, the assets related to the natural gas transportation, the conditioning and processing of natural gas retained in plant for the separation and fractionation of gasoline, propane and butane, the storage of the produced natural gas, and the
commercial and technical operation of the LNG regasification terminal in Escobar, which were formerly included in the Gas and Power business segment, were assigned to this business segment. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are mainly derived from the sale of crude oil, refined and petrochemical products, and specialties for agribusiness industry
and grains and their <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">by-products,</FONT> through the businesses of B2C (Retail), B2B (Commercial Networks, Industries, Transportation, Aviation, Agro, Lubricants and Specialties), LPG, Chemicals, International Trade
and Transportation and Sales to Companies. In addition, it obtains revenues from midstream oil, midstream gas and natural gas storage operations and the provision of LNG regasification services. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the aforementioned activities, including the purchase of: (i)&nbsp;crude oil from the Upstream business
segment and third parties; (ii)&nbsp;natural gas to be consumed in the refinery and petrochemical industrial complexes from the LNG and Integrated Gas business segment; and (iii)&nbsp;natural gas retained in plant from the Upstream business segment.

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;natural gas transportation and commercialization to third parties and to the Midstream and

venture Mega; and (iii)&nbsp;the development of LNG capacity. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;1, 2025, as a consequence of the organizational changes
described above, the assets related to the natural gas transportation, the conditioning and processing of natural gas retained in plant for the separation and fractionation of gasoline, propane and butane, the storage of the produced natural gas,
and the commercial and technical operation of the LNG regasification terminal in Escobar, which were formerly included in the Gas and Power business segment, were assigned to the Midstream and Downstream business segment. Furthermore, the assets
related to the distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas, the generation of conventional thermal electric power and renewable energy, and the production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers through our investments in
associates and joint ventures, which were formerly included in the Gas and Power business segment, were assigned to the New Energies business segment. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are mainly derived from the commercialization of natural gas as producers to third parties and to the Midstream and
Downstream and the New Energies business segments. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the aforementioned activities, including the
purchase of natural gas from the Upstream business segment. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;1, 2025, as a consequence of the organizational changes described above, the New Energies Vice Presidency was created and
during the current fiscal year the complete management scope of this new business unit was determined. As of that date, the assets related to the distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas, the generation of conventional thermal
electric power and renewable energy and the production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers through our investments in associates and joint ventures, which were formerly included in the Gas and Power business segment, were assigned to this
business segment. In addition, the assets related to the provision of research and development services of technology applied to the hydrocarbon industry through our subsidiary <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Y-TEC,</FONT> previously included in
Central Administration and Others, were assigned to this business segment. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;the definition
and development of the new energy portfolio; (ii)&nbsp;the definition and development of sustainability and energy transitions programs; (iii)&nbsp;the distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas; and (iv)&nbsp;the provision of
research and development services of technology applied to the hydrocarbon industry through our subsidiary <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Y-TEC.</FONT> Furthermore, through our investments in associates and joint ventures, this business segment
performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;the generation of conventional thermal electric power and renewable energy; and (ii)&nbsp;the production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are mainly derived from the sale of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the aforementioned activities, including the purchase of natural gas from the LNG and Integrated Gas

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It includes the remaining activities performed by the Group that do not fall within the aforementioned business segments and which are not
reporting business segments, mainly comprising revenues, expenses and assets related to: (i)&nbsp;corporate administrative; (ii)&nbsp;the production of frac sand for well drilling/fracking purposes; and (iii)&nbsp;the construction activities through
our subsidiary AESA. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;1, 2024, certain assets related to the production of frac sand for well drilling/fracking purposes,

Energies business segment. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Sales between business segments were made at internal transfer prices established by the Group, which approximately
reflect domestic market prices. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Operating profit or loss and assets of each business segment have been determined after consolidation adjustments.

Brasil&#8221;)&#8221; section. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><U>Mature Fields Project </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The
Mature Fields Project is described in Note 11 &#8220;Mature Fields Project&#8221; section to the annual consolidated financial statements. Updates for the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2025, are described below: </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Description of the Mature Fields Project </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The assignment agreements that met the agreed closing conditions during the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2025, and therefore the transaction was settled are
described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><U>Estaci&oacute;n Fern&aacute;ndez Oro </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">On December&nbsp;19,
2024, Decree No.&nbsp;525/2024 was published in the Official Gazette of the Province of R&iacute;o Negro, which authorized the transfer of 100% of YPF&#8217;s rights and obligations in the &#8220;Estaci&oacute;n Fern&aacute;ndez Oro&#8221;
exploitation concession in favor of Quintana E&amp;P Argentina S.R.L., Quintana Energy Investments S.A., and Gas Storage and Midstream Services S.A. (&#8220;Quintana Consortium&#8221;). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">On February&nbsp;3, 2025, after the fulfillment of the closing conditions by YPF and Quintana Consortium, the transfer of 100% of the rights and obligations of YPF in
such exploitation concession in favor of Quintana Consortium was formalized. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><U>Campamento Central - Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Perdido </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">On January&nbsp;6, 2025, Decree No.&nbsp;1,892/2024 was published in the Official Gazette of the Province of Chubut, which authorized the transfer of 100% of the rights
and obligations in the &#8220;Campamento Central - Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Perdido&#8221; exploitation concession, in which YPF held a working interest of 50%, in favor of PECOM Servicios Energ&iacute;a S.A.U. (&#8220;PECOM&#8221;). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">On January&nbsp;31, 2025, after the fulfillment of the closing conditions by YPF and PECOM, the transfer of 100% of the rights and obligations of YPF in such exploitation
concession in favor of PECOM was formalized. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><U>Barrancas, Vizcacheras, La Ventana, Ceferino, Mesa Verde and R&iacute;o Tunuy&aacute;n</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">On January&nbsp;29, 2025, Resolution No.&nbsp;16/2025 was published in the Official Gazette of the Province of Mendoza, which authorized the transfer of 100% of
YPF&#8217;s rights and obligations in &#8220;Barrancas&#8221;, &#8220;Vizcacheras&#8221;, &#8220;La Ventana&#8221;, &#8220;Ceferino&#8221;, &#8220;Mesa Verde&#8221; and &#8220;R&iacute;o Tunuy&aacute;n&#8221; exploitation concessions in favor of
Petr&oacute;leos Sudamericanos S.A. (&#8220;PS&#8221;). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">On March&nbsp;27, 2025, after the fulfillment of the closing conditions by YPF and PS, the transfer of 100%
of the rights and obligations of YPF in such exploitation concessions in favor of PS was formalized with effective date as of April&nbsp;1, 2025. </P>

addition, the Company maintains groups of assets as held for sale for which agreements have not yet been signed but continues in negotiations with third parties for their disposal or reversal. The delay in the fulfillment of the plan for the

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>12. ASSETS HELD FOR SALE AND ASSOCIATED LIABILITIES (cont.) </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Based on the assessment of the changes in the fair value, the Company recognized a loss due to changes in the fair value of assets held for sale of
260,132 in the &#8220;Other net operating results&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income, mainly associated with expenses of various nature arising from the general terms and conditions of the MOU signed with the Province of Santa
Cruz and Fomicruz. Additionally, in relation to aforementioned MOU, YPF recognized a liability in the &#8220;Liabilities under agreements&#8221; line under the &#8220;Other liabilities&#8221; line item in the statement of financial position related
to (i)&nbsp;the execution of an environmental remediation and abandonment program, and (ii)&nbsp;the payment of a compensatory bonus to the Province of Santa Cruz. As of September&nbsp;30, 2025, the balance of this liability amounts to 497,014. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Based on the fair value of the groups of assets at the closing date of each of the assignment agreements mentioned in the &#8220;Description of the
Mature Fields Project&#8221; section, YPF additionally recognized a gain on the sale of such groups of assets amounts to a gain of 223,556. The total consideration agreed includes cash payment of US$ 63&nbsp;million and crude oil deliveries for a
period of 4 years as payment in kind. Additionally, the derecognition of the carrying amount of the liabilities directly associated with assets held for sale net of the assets held for sale related to such exploitation concessions was 621,773. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Additionally, in relation to the Mature Fields Project, for the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2025, the Company: </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The effective income tax rate projected at the end of the fiscal year amounts to 125.7%. The variation in this rate compared to the effective rate as of
December&nbsp;31, 2024 (see Note 18 to the annual consolidated financial statements) is mainly explained by the impact of the estimation of certain macroeconomic variables in the measurement of property, plant, and equipment for accounting and tax
purposes, which generates an increase in deferred income tax liability related to those assets. The accounting measurement of property, plant and equipment is based on the Company&#8217;s functional currency according to IFRS (see Note 2.b)), while
the tax measurement is based on inflation-adjusted pesos. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of September&nbsp;30, 2025 and December&nbsp;31, 2024, the causes that generated charges
within &#8220;Other comprehensive income&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income did not generate temporary differences subject to income tax. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of September&nbsp;30, 2025 and December&nbsp;31, 2024 the Group has classified as deferred tax asset 6,043 and 339,492, respectively, and as deferred
tax liability 535,530 and 92,701, respectively, all of which arise from the net deferred tax balances of each of the individual companies included in these condensed interim consolidated financial statements. </P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="left"><B>SHAREHOLDERS&#8217; EQUITY </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of September&nbsp;30, 2025, the Company&#8217;s capital amounts to 3,928 and treasury shares amount to 5 represented by 393,312,793 book-entry shares
of common stock and divided into four classes of shares (A, B, C and D), with a par value of 10 pesos and 1 vote per share. These shares are fully subscribed, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">paid-in</FONT> and authorized for stock exchange listing.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of September&nbsp;30, 2025, there are 3,764 Class&nbsp;A outstanding shares. As long as any Class&nbsp;A share remains outstanding, the
affirmative vote of the Argentine Government is required for: (i)&nbsp;mergers; (ii) acquisitions of more than 50% of YPF shares in an agreed or hostile bid; (iii)&nbsp;transfers of all the YPF&#8217;s exploitation and exploration rights;
(iv)&nbsp;the voluntary dissolution of YPF; (v)&nbsp;change of corporate and/or tax address outside Argentina; or (vi)&nbsp;make an acquisition that would result in the purchaser holding 15% or more of the Company&#8217;s capital stock, or 20% or
more of the outstanding Class&nbsp;D shares. Items (iii)&nbsp;and (iv) also require prior approval by the Argentine Congress. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the nine-month
periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2025 and 2024, the Company has not repurchased any of its own shares. Furthermore, on October&nbsp;14, 2025, the Company repurchased 343,654 of its own shares issued for an amount of 10 for purposes of compliance
with the share-based benefit plans. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;30, 2025, the General Shareholders&#8217; Meeting was held, which approved the statutory financial
statements of YPF (see Note 2.b)) corresponding to the year ended on December&nbsp;31, 2024 and, additionally, approved the following in relation to the retained earnings: (i)&nbsp;completely release the reserve for purchase of treasury shares and
the reserve for investments; (ii)&nbsp;allocate the amount of 34,205 to appropriate a reserve for purchase of treasury shares; and (iii)&nbsp;allocate the amount of 6,787,343 to appropriate a reserve for investments. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>34.a) Contingent assets </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL">The Group has no significant contingent assets. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>34.b) Contingent liabilities
</B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Contingent liabilities are described in Note 34.b) to the annual consolidated financial statements. Updates for the nine-month period ended
September&nbsp;30, 2025, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>34.b.1) Contentious claims </B></P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Petersen Energ&iacute;a Inversora, S.A.U. and Petersen Energ&iacute;a, S.A.U. (collectively, &#8220;Petersen&#8221;)
&#8211; Eton Park Capital Management, L.P., Eton Park Master Fund, LTD. and Eton Park Fund, L.P. (collectively, &#8220;Eton Park&#8221;, and together with Petersen, the &#8220;Plaintiffs&#8221;)</B> </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;30, 2025, the District Court granted Plaintiffs&#8217; turnover motion, ordering the Republic to: (i)&nbsp;transfer its Class&nbsp;D shares
of YPF to a global custody account at the Bank of New York Mellon (&#8220;BNYM&#8221;) in New York within 14 days of the date of the order; and (ii)&nbsp;instruct BNYM to initiate a transfer of the Republic&#8217;s ownership interests in its
Class&nbsp;D shares of YPF to Plaintiffs or their designees within one business day of the date on which the shares are deposited into the account. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Also on June&nbsp;30, 2025, in proceedings brought by Bainbridge Fund Ltd. against the Republic, the District Court issued a similar order directing the
Republic to turn over its Class&nbsp;A and Class&nbsp;D shares of YPF. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Republic filed motions to stay the June&nbsp;30, 2025 turnover orders
pending its appeal of those orders, which were denied by the District Court. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;10, 2025, the Republic filed with the Court of Appeals:
(i)&nbsp;notices of appeal of the June&nbsp;30, 2025 turnover orders in both Plaintiffs&#8217; and Bainbridge Fund Ltd.&#8217;s proceedings; and (ii)&nbsp;emergency motions for a stay pending appeal of the June&nbsp;30, 2025 turnover orders and an
immediate administrative stay. On July&nbsp;15, 2025, the Court of Appeals granted a temporary administrative stay of the turnover orders pending resolution of the stay motions. On August&nbsp;15, 2025, the Court of Appeals granted a stay pending
resolution of the Republic&#8217;s appeal of the June&nbsp;30, 2025 turnover orders. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">YPF is not a party to the aforementioned turnover proceedings.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;29, 2025, the District Court lifted the stay of alter ego discovery entered on November&nbsp;15, 2024, including regarding YPF. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On September&nbsp;17, 2025, the District Court denied YPF&#8217;s request to permanently enjoin Plaintiffs from pursuing recovery from YPF in connection
with their September&nbsp;15, 2023 final judgment against the Republic and ordered Plaintiffs and YPF to continue with the discovery process. It should be noted that the District Court&#8217;s decision does not decide the question of whether YPF is
an alter ego of the Republic, which YPF strongly denies. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On October&nbsp;1, 2025, YPF filed a motion for reconsideration of the September&nbsp;17,
2025 order with the District Court, as well as a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-motion</FONT> letter requesting to stay discovery from YPF. On October&nbsp;6, 2025, Plaintiffs submitted a letter opposing a discovery stay and YPF replied on
October&nbsp;7, 2025. On October&nbsp;15, 2025, Plaintiffs filed an opposition to YPF&#8217;s motion for reconsideration. On October&nbsp;16, 2025, the District Court held a conference regarding YPF&#8217;s request to stay alter ego discovery from
YPF. The Court granted the request for a stay pending resolution of YPF&#8217;s reconsideration motion. On October&nbsp;17, 2025, YPF filed its notice of appeal of the September&nbsp;17, 2025 order. On October&nbsp;22, 2025, YPF filed its reply to
Plaintiffs&#8217; opposition of October&nbsp;15, 2025. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">With respect to the appeal of the final judgment issued on September&nbsp;15, 2023, the Court
of Appeals held oral argument on October&nbsp;29, 2025. </P>

conditions, the Bareboat Charter Agreement with Golar MKII Corporation became effective. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In order to supply the FLNG Hilli and FLNG
MKII vessels with natural gas for the liquefaction process, SESA entered into natural gas supply agreements (&#8220;GSA&#8221;) with PAE, Sur Inversiones Energ&eacute;ticas, Pampa and Wintershall for the term of 20 years (see Note 36.f)). In this
regard, in order for both vessels to operate all year round, SESA contemplates the construction of a dedicated gas pipeline between the Province of Neuqu&eacute;n and the San Mat&iacute;as Gulf in the Province of R&iacute;o Negro. Operations of the
FLNG Hilli vessel are expected to commence in late 2027 or early 2028 and those of the FLNG MKII vessel are expected to commence in late 2028. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of
the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the shareholding in SESA is as follows: PAE (30%); Sur Inversiones Energ&eacute;ticas (25%); Pampa (20%); SE Argentina Holding B.V., by transfer from Wintershall on
July&nbsp;24, 2025 (15%); and Golar Subholding (10%). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company has entered into the GSA and the SESA Shareholders&#8217; Agreement guaranteeing
the obligations of its subsidiary Sur Inversiones Energ&eacute;ticas under such agreements. In addition, related to the 25% equity interest of Sur Inversiones Energ&eacute;ticas in SESA, on May&nbsp;30, 2025, and October&nbsp;27, 2025, the Company
granted guarantees in favor of Golar Hilli Corporation for up to US$ 137.5&nbsp;million and in favor of Golar MKII Corporation for up to US$ 187.5&nbsp;million, respectively. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.c) Granted guarantees </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Vaca Muerta Sur
Project guarantee</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;8, 2025, our associated VMOS signed an international syndicated loan for US$ 2,000&nbsp;million to finance the
construction of the Vaca Muerta Sur Project. As guarantee for the obligations assumed in this loan, VMOS&#8217;s shareholders, including YPF, have granted a fiduciary assignment of their VMOS&#8217;s shares as collateral for such financing, which
will remain in force until the completion of the Vaca Muerta Sur Project. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:48pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.a) Regulations applicable to the hydrocarbon industry </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2025, there were no significant updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 36.a) to the
annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.b) Regulations applicable to the Midstream and Downstream business segment </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Notes 36.b), 36.c.1), 36.c.2) and 36.c.4) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the
nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2025, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.b.1) Regulatory framework associated with the LPG industry </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;3, 2025, Decree No.&nbsp;446/2025 was published modifying the LPG Law, which: (i)&nbsp;confirms the free import of LPG; (ii)&nbsp;removes the
authority of the PEN to impose restrictions on prices and commercialization conditions; and (iii)&nbsp;limits the intervention of the SE in the LPG industry to technical and safety aspects.&#8195; </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.c) Regulations applicable to the LNG and Integrated Gas business segment </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Notes 36.c.1) and 36.c.2) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the nine-month period ended
September&nbsp;30, 2025, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.c.1) Exports of natural gas and LNG </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>LNG</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;21, 2025, SE Resolution
No.&nbsp;157/2025 was published, which approved the declaration of sufficiency of natural gas resources in Argentina that would supply local demand and LNG export projects for 63 years, which must be updated by the SE at least every 5 years. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.d) Regulations applicable to the New Energies business segment </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Notes 36.c.3), 36.c.5) and 36.c.6) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the nine-month
period ended September&nbsp;30, 2025, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.d.1) Regulatory requirements applicable to natural gas distribution </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Tariff schemes and tariff renegotiations</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">ENARGAS, through several resolutions, approved the transition tariff schemes to be applied by Metrogas until the rates resulting from the RQT came into
force in accordance with the provisions of Decree No.&nbsp;55/2023. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;30, 2025, ENARGAS Resolution No.&nbsp;257/2025 was published, which
approved: (i)&nbsp;the RQT corresponding to Metrogas; (ii)&nbsp;the segmentation of residential users; (iii)&nbsp;the investment plans for the five-year period 2025 - 2030; and (iv)&nbsp;the initial tariff scheme and the schemes of rates and charges
corresponding to Metrogas effective as from May&nbsp;1, 2025. The increase expected as a result of the RQT process will be effective in 31 consecutive monthly increases, which recognizes a cost for the deferral at a real weighted average cost of the
capital employed rate in pesos of 7.64% and establishes that the increase in distribution tariffs for May 2025 applicable to residential users and general service customers will be 3%. The application of the remaining increase derived from the RQT
will be completed in the remaining 30 installments, plus the recognition of the cost of the aforementioned deferral. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;5, 2025, SE
Resolution No.&nbsp;241/2025 was published, which established that the transportation and distribution tariffs will be adjusted on a monthly basis according to the variations in the indexes established by ENARGAS in the RQT, which correspond to the
variation in equal parts of the IPC and the Internal Wholesale Price Index (&#8220;IPIM&#8221; by its acronym in Spanish) published by the INDEC. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;6, 2025, ENARGAS Resolution No.&nbsp;363/2025 was published, which approved: (i)&nbsp;the
methodology for the monthly adjustment of tariffs; and (ii)&nbsp;the tariff charts to be applied by Metrogas effective as from June&nbsp;6, 2025. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">ENARGAS, through several resolutions, approved the tariff schemes to be applied by Metrogas on a monthly basis within the framework of the RQT in
accordance with the provisions of ENARGAS Resolution No. 363/2025.<U>Procedure for the compensation of the lower revenues received by natural gas distributors from their users</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;31, 2025, SE Resolution No.&nbsp;24/2025 repealed as from February&nbsp;1, 2025 MINEM Resolution No.
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">508-E/2017,</FONT> which established the procedure to compensate natural gas distributors for lower revenues due to benefits and/or bonuses and higher costs of UNG and unified the compensation mechanisms for lower
revenues received as a consequence of the application of incentive programs involving bonuses on the price of natural gas in the PIST. The amounts to be compensated will be deducted from the amounts to be paid by distributors to natural gas
producers and will be directly compensated by the SE through the Plan GasAr 2023-2028. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.d.2) Regulatory framework associated with electric
power generation </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;7, 2025, Decree No.&nbsp;450/2025 was published, which approves the following amendments to the Regulatory
Framework associated with electric power generation: (i)&nbsp;maximum competition and free contracting is guaranteed to generators; (ii)&nbsp;supply contracts will be freely negotiated between the parties; (iii)&nbsp;the figure of
&#8220;storer&#8221; is introduced as the owner of energy storage facilities; (iv)&nbsp;the figure of &#8220;free user&#8221; is introduced, who, together with large users, may contract independently and for own consumption the energy supply;
(v)&nbsp;allows the PEN to authorize generators, distributors and/or large users to build, at their exclusive cost and to satisfy their own needs, a line and/or extension of the transmission grid, which will not provide a public transportation
service; and (vi)&nbsp;the extensions of the Argentine Electricity Grid (&#8220;SADI&#8221;, by its acronym in Spanish) may be of free initiative and at the own risk of whoever executes them. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><U>CAMMESA </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The SE, through several complementary notes to SE
Resolution No.&nbsp;21/2025, informed CAMMESA of the &#8220;Guidelines for the Standardization of the WEM and its Progressive Adaptation&#8221;, which details among others the modifications foreseen for the management of fuels, the determination of
prices and the operation of the term market and the spot market, approved by SE Resolution No.&nbsp;400/2025 and applicable as from November&nbsp;1, 2025. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.d.3) Decree No.&nbsp;55/2023 &#8220;Emergency in the National Energy Sector&#8221; </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;2, 2025, Decree No.&nbsp;370/2025 was published extending the emergency of the national energy sector until July&nbsp;9, 2026. It also
provided for the extension of the intervention of ENRE and ENARGAS until July&nbsp;9, 2026 or until the constitution, commencement and appointment of the members of the Board of Directors of the National Gas and Electricity Regulatory Agency. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;7, 2025, Decree No.&nbsp;452/2025 was published, establishing the National Gas and Electricity Regulatory Agency and granting a term of 180
days for its commencement of operations. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.e) Incentive programs for hydrocarbon production </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 36.d) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the nine-month period ended
September&nbsp;30, 2025, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.e.1) Incentive programs for natural gas production </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Plan for Reinsurance and Promotion of Federal Hydrocarbon Production Domestic Self-Sufficiency, Exports, Imports Substitution and the Expansion of the
Transportation System for all Hydrocarbon Basins in the Country 2023-2028 (&#8220;Plan GasAr 2023-2028&#8221;)</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The SE, through several
resolutions, approves the natural gas prices at the PIST to be passed-through to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">end-users</FONT> in connection with current contracts entered into within the framework of the Plan GasAr 2023-2028. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 36.g) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the nine-month period ended
September&nbsp;30, 2025, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.h.1) Export duties </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Agricultural products</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;31, 2025,
Decree No.&nbsp;526/2025 was published, which established the permanent reduction in export duties established by Decree No.&nbsp;38/2025. As from such date, the rates are set at 26% for soybean, 24.5% for soybean byproducts such as soybean oil and
soybean meal, and 9.5% for grains such as wheat, corn and sorghum. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.i) Regulations related to the Foreign Exchange Market </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 36.h) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the nine-month period ended
September&nbsp;30, 2025, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;11, 2025, the Argentine Government announced measures to loosen the foreign exchange
regime and reinforce the monetary framework. By virtue of this, the BCRA implemented a new foreign exchange regime in which certain restrictions to access the Foreign Exchange Market were eliminated. The following are the main measures: (i)&nbsp;the
&#8220;crawling peg&#8221; adjustment mechanism is eliminated and the dollar exchange rate in the Foreign Exchange Market may fluctuate in a range between 1,000 pesos and 1,400 pesos, whose limits will be increased at a rate of 1% per month;
(ii)&nbsp;the &#8220;blend&#8221; dollar was eliminated (see Note 36.i) &#8220;Export Increase Program&#8221; section); (iii) certain foreign exchange restrictions to individuals for the purchase of foreign currency were eliminated; (iv)&nbsp;access
to the Foreign Exchange Market is allowed without prior approval of the BCRA for the payment of dividends to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-resident</FONT> shareholders accrued as from fiscal years beginning on or after January&nbsp;1, 2025;
and (v)&nbsp;the terms for the payment of foreign trade transactions are flexibilized, eliminating the schedule established by the BCRA for access to the Foreign Exchange Market without prior approval for the payment of imports of goods with customs
entry registration as from December&nbsp;13, 2023 and of services rendered and/or accrued as from such date. </P>

</P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item273667_44"></A>38. EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLANS AND SIMILAR OBLIGATIONS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Note 38 to the annual consolidated financial statements describes the main characteristics and accounting treatment for employee benefit plans and similar
obligations implemented by the Group. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Retirement plan</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense related to the Retirement Plan was 3,801 and 2,890 for the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2025 and 2024,
respectively. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Short-term benefit programs</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense related to the short-term benefit programs was 181,584 and 152,788 for the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2025
and 2024, respectively. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Share-based benefit plans</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of September&nbsp;30, 2025, there are 4.6&nbsp;million number of PSARs outstanding with and a weighted average fair value of US$ 10.87 per PSARs. The
amount charged to expense in relation with Value Generation Plan was a recovery of 9,582 due to changes in the fair value estimate of the option and a loss of 6,762 for the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2025 and 2024, respectively. As
of December&nbsp;31, 2024, weighted average fair value was US$ 28.6 per PSARs. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense in relation with the remaining
share-based benefit plans was 10,341 and 4,119 to be settled in equity instruments, for the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2025 and 2024, respectively, and 1,583 and 8,395 to be settled in cash, for the nine-month periods ended
September&nbsp;30, 2025 and 2024, respectively. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Note 2.b.11) to the annual consolidated financial statements describes the accounting policies for
share-based benefit plans. Repurchases of treasury shares are disclosed in Note 32. </P>
